summary: Reviewed the walk-in launch changes across booking APIs, launch copy, customer-facing content, and tests. The public proxy now strips retired Sunday-lunch fields and service-window checks generally fail closed, but several unhappy-path workflows still risk failed bookings or misleading customers. The most material risks are stale legacy booking clients, incomplete agent large-group payment handling, and public content that still describes the retired pre-order/cutoff model.
appears_sound: The public `/api/table-bookings` normalisation strips inbound `sunday_lunch`, `booking_type`, and menu-selection fields before forwarding `booking_type: 'regular'` in `app/api/table-bookings/route.ts`.

Service-window validation happens before upstream booking creation in both public and agent POST paths, and hours lookup failure returns 503 rather than creating an unchecked booking in `app/api/table-bookings/route.ts` and `app/api/booking/agent/route.ts`.

`LaunchAnnouncementClient` handles the three launch states and clears its interval on unmount; tests cover pre-launch, launch-day, post-expiry, and interval switching in `components/announcements/__tests__/LaunchAnnouncement.test.tsx`.
The PayPal recovery path is covered for the main customer form: `tests/unit/ManagementTableBookingForm.test.tsx` verifies `fallback_payment_url` renders when inline PayPal setup fails.

findings.description: Failure sequence: a user has an old cached booking wizard or non-JS form open, completes the booking, and submits to `/api/booking/submit`; after this deletion the route 404s instead of translating the request into the new `/api/table-bookings` path. The booking fails after the user has entered all details, with no compatibility shim or recovery route in the pack.
findings.evidence: `app/api/booking/submit/route.ts` is deleted; the removed handler previously accepted JSON and form submissions, ran validation/service-window checks, and called `anchorAPI.createTableBooking`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: If no deployed or external clients can still post to this endpoint, the current UI may be unaffected.
findings.what_would_confirm: Check deployed access logs and built client bundles for `/api/booking/submit`, or add a temporary shim and verify stale payloads are accepted.

findings.description: Failure sequence: an AI agent posts a booking, the upstream create succeeds, the network drops before the response, and the agent retries; this handler appears to call booking creation again without a stable idempotency key. That can create duplicate table bookings or holds for the same customer and slot.
findings.evidence: The agent POST handler calls `anchorAPI.createTableBooking(bookingRequest)` with no idempotency argument or request-header idempotency handling visible in the pack.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: `anchorAPI.createTableBooking` might generate and persist a stable idempotency key internally, but its method body is not included in the visible pack excerpt.
findings.what_would_confirm: Test two identical agent POST retries and verify the management API receives the same `Idempotency-Key` or returns one booking.

findings.description: Failure sequence: an agent books a party of 10+, management returns a `pending_payment` state or payment URL, but this endpoint still returns `success: true` with booking-confirmed copy and no actionable payment URL branch. The customer can believe the booking is complete while the hold later expires unpaid.
findings.evidence: After `createTableBooking`, the response always builds `success: true` and `message: Booking confirmed...`; the only large-group branch is the text `specialInstructions` copy at `app/api/booking/agent/route.ts:149`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The management API may send an SMS or out-of-band payment link for AI-agent bookings, but that contract is not shown in the pack.
findings.what_would_confirm: Add a route test where `createTableBooking` resolves `status: 'pending_payment'` with `next_step_url` or `fallback_payment_url` and assert the agent response exposes a payment-required workflow.

findings.description: Failure sequence: a customer researching Sunday lunch reads retained pre-order, Saturday-cutoff, or universal-deposit copy, assumes the new walk-in flow is unavailable or that a small party must pay, and abandons or calls unnecessarily. This conflicts with the launch workflow that removed Sunday pre-orders/cutoffs and moved deposits to groups of 10+ only.
findings.evidence: `content/blog/best-sunday-roast-surrey/index.md:31` still lists The Anchor booking as `Yes (by Sat 1pm)`, and `content/blog/60th-birthday-party-ideas-venues/index.md:43` says Sunday lunch requires advance booking, a per-person deposit, and a Saturday 1pm deadline.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: Some affected pages may be archive content, but they are still public customer-visible surfaces in the changed pack.

findings.description: Failure sequence: `/sunday-lunch` is cached before 17 May with pre-launch HTML, then a user opens it after cutover; the client component initializes from `Date.now()` instead of a server-provided initial value, so the first browser render can disagree with cached HTML before the interval repair. That risks a hydration warning and stale or flashing copy during the exact launch transition.
findings.evidence: `SundayLunchHowItWorks` initializes state with `useState<string>(() => pickBody(Date.now()))` while its comment claims cached pages should flip safely.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: Next.js deployment mode may avoid prerendering this client component in a way that produces a visible mismatch.
findings.what_would_confirm: Render a pre-launch static page, hydrate it with `Date.now()` after `WALK_IN_LAUNCH_STARTS_AT_MS`, and check for hydration mismatch or visible flash.

findings.description: Failure sequence: an AI assistant consumes `llms.txt`, tells a customer Sunday opening is until 9pm or Saturday kitchen runs until 9pm, and the customer arrives outside the actual published service window. This creates a stale-data failure path for AI-mediated visits even though the human-facing copy-assumptions source says Sunday is 1pm-6pm and Saturday kitchen is 1pm-7pm.
findings.evidence: `public/llms.txt:24` says `Sunday: 12pm-9pm`, and `public/llms.txt:29` says `Saturday: 12pm-9pm` for kitchen hours, conflicting with `docs/copy-assumptions.md:18` and `docs/copy-assumptions.md:19`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: If `llms.txt` intentionally uses a different operational source than `docs/copy-assumptions.md`, the source of truth needs to be clarified.

empty_categories: No remaining Saturday-1pm cutoff branch found in the changed public booking API handlers included in the pack.
No hostile inbound `sunday_lunch` or `booking_type` forwarding found in the new public `/api/table-bookings` proxy path.
No unmount cleanup leak found in `LaunchAnnouncementClient`; the interval is cleared in the effect cleanup.
No service-window fail-open found in the changed POST handlers; failure to verify hours returns before upstream booking creation.
No PayPal fallback UI gap found for the tested main-form inline-PayPal-failure path; `fallback_payment_url` is rendered as a recovery link.
